item.title: Forking a prebuilt wheel package to support newer Python versions because the upstream stopped updating (Pyopenjtalk)
item.description:
Note: I’m based in Korea, so some context here is Korea-specific.

A while back I wrote a post about building a TTS with Bert-VITS2 . I’ve been using that TTS pretty happily ever since. But… the Bert-VITS2 repo development just stopped.

When a repo stops getting updates, what’s the problem? Bumping Python versions and managing dependencies becomes painful.

In my case, I have an “ML Server” on my home server where I’ve crammed all my ML-related stuff. So I’ve installed all sorts of things on it… and when there’s a stale repo like that, conflicts keep popping up whenever I try to install something. For example, numpy 2.0…

item.title: Use AWS Resources from GitHub Actions Without AWS Keys via GitHub OIDC (Free)
item.description:
Note: I’m based in Korea, so some context here is Korea-specific.

To use AWS from GitHub Actions, you typically go through the following steps.

  • Go to the IAM console and create a new user.
  • Add an IAM Role for GitHub Actions and use Programmatic access to issue an AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
  • In your repository settings, add the freshly issued AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY to GitHub Secrets.
  • Then add a workflow like the one below in GitHub Actions to access AWS resources.
yaml 
- name: Configure AWS Credentials
 uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v1
 with:
 aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
 aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
 aws-region: us-east-2

If you only have one project, managing things this way isn’t a big problem.
